title: Best concealer 2026: dark circles and blemishes
description: The $11 drugstore concealer and the $35 luxury one. Compared on coverage, shade depth and the creasing owners report by mid-afternoon.
lede: The $11 drugstore concealer and the $35 luxury one. Compared on coverage, shade depth and the creasing owners report by mid-afternoon.

sections.heading: How we compared
paragraphs: Each concealer is compared on the same two jobs it is bought for: covering under-eye darkness and covering a blemish. The points that separate them are coverage at application, creasing under the eye around the four-hour mark (the most common concealer failure point), how long blemish coverage holds through a working day, and shade range including depth and undertone options.

Shade range is judged across the full published range of each line, with particular attention to whether the deep end is genuinely deep rather than a repeat of the medium shades — the failure mode buyers with deeper skin describe most often.
Here's the summary before the detail:

| Concealer | Price | Shades | Coverage | Creasing reports (4h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tarte Shape Tape | $29 | 30 | High | Mild |
| NARS Radiant Creamy | $33 | 30 | Medium-full | None |
| Charlotte Tilbury Magic Away | $35 | 18 | Full | None |
| Rare Beauty Liquid Touch | $22 | 48 | Medium | None |
| Maybelline Instant Age Rewind | $11 | 20 | Medium | Mild |

Creasing reflects how often owners describe creasing at the four-hour mark without setting powder: None (essentially unreported), Mild (occasional), Moderate (frequent), Severe (the dominant complaint).

sections.heading: Tarte Shape Tape — the cult classic revisited
paragraphs: Shape Tape built its reputation on coverage intensity, and owner reviews back it up: full coverage in one application over blemishes, with dark circle coverage buyers describe as holding through a full working day. The flat doe-foot applicator deposits a generous amount that blends cleanly with either a brush or a fingertip.

The creasing question is where Shape Tape has earned criticism: owners regularly describe mild creasing under the eye by the four-hour mark with no powder, and report that a light dusting of translucent powder holds it off through the day. Setting powder is effectively required for under-eye use — which is a step the NARS and Charlotte Tilbury don't need.

Thirty shades is adequate but limited at the deep end. The deepest shade (53S) is lighter than NARS's Syracuse or the Rare Beauty deep options. Worth noting for deeper skin tones. At $29 it's competitive pricing for the coverage intensity.

sections.heading: NARS Radiant Creamy — best for natural under-eye coverage
paragraphs: The NARS Radiant Creamy Concealer's luminous finish brightens the under-eye area rather than just covering it, which is a different result than the other four formulas here.

Coverage is medium-buildable — applying a second coat reaches medium-full. It's not the concealer to use over significant blemishes without a second coat; owners report a single pass leaving partial coverage on a moderate breakout. Where it excels is the specific under-eye use case: dark circles, fine lines, and the general shadowing that makes you look tired.

Thirty shades — similar range to Shape Tape, with a slightly better selection of undertones in the 30s-40s (in terms of standard shade numbering). At $33 it's the most expensive formula-per-function here: you're paying for the under-eye formula specifically.

sections.heading: Charlotte Tilbury Magic Away — best no-crease full coverage
paragraphs: The Magic Away formula addresses the coverage vs. creasing trade-off better than any other concealer here: owner reviews describe full coverage at application and no creasing at the four- or eight-hour mark, with no setting powder. How it does this without the sticky or cakey texture that usually comes with full coverage is the formula's actual achievement.

The limitation is shade range. Eighteen shades is the lowest of all five here, and the shade progression skips options in the medium-deep range. Buyers with deeper skin regularly report finding no close match in the Magic Away line. If you're in the 30s-40s shade range (light-medium), you have options; darker needs are underserved.

At $35 you're paying for the crease-free full coverage formula. For light-to-medium skin covering blemishes, dark circles, and redness without a setting powder step, this is the most efficient single product in the group.

sections.heading: Rare Beauty Liquid Touch — best shade range
paragraphs: Forty-eight shades makes the Rare Beauty Liquid Touch the most inclusive concealer in this comparison — and those shades include genuine depth in the medium-dark to deep range. It is the one formula here that buyers with deeper skin consistently report matching quickly, where Shape Tape and Charlotte Tilbury draw the opposite complaint.

The coverage is medium — intentionally so. The formula is designed to look like skin rather than cover it, which means texture and fine lines stay visible after application. For dark circles and general evening, that's often preferable. For covering significant blemishes, you need two coats and possibly a concealer pen on top for spot coverage.

The flexible finish won't emphasize fine texture, which is useful for mature skin and around the eyes. Creasing at the four-hour mark is essentially absent from owner reviews. At $22 it's mid-tier pricing with the widest shade range in this group — the best starting point for anyone who has struggled with shade matching.

sections.heading: Maybelline Instant Age Rewind — best drugstore dark circle pick
paragraphs: The Instant Age Rewind's eraser sponge tip deposits a peach-toned brightening formula that works specifically for blue or purple under-eye circles. Peach color-correction neutralizes the blue undertone before coverage, which is why a $11 product can compete with $30+ options on the specific dark circle use case.

Coverage is medium. On blemishes, owners report one pass leaving some redness visible at the edges. On dark circles, buyers with neutral-to-warm undertones rate the peach correction plus coverage on a par with the NARS. On cool undertone skin the peach corrector reads slightly orange — keep that in mind when testing.

Creasing at the four-hour mark with no setting powder is a recurring complaint, as it is with Shape Tape. Apply with a brush for better control than the sponge tip applicator, which can over-apply. At $11 it's the one to buy if dark circles are your primary concern and budget is a factor.

faqs.q: Should concealer be lighter or darker than my foundation?
faqs.a: For under-eye use, go one shade lighter to counteract the natural shadow. For blemish coverage, match your foundation shade exactly — a lighter shade makes blemishes look highlighted rather than covered. If you're buying one concealer for both uses, pick your foundation match and use color-correcting technique (peach or orange corrector) for dark circles.

faqs.q: Why does concealer crease under my eyes?
faqs.a: Two main causes: applying too much product, and using a dry-finish formula that sets in the natural creases of the under-eye. Apply in thin layers, and use a setting powder specifically designed for under-eyes (translucent, finely milled). NARS Radiant Creamy and Charlotte Tilbury Magic Away are the two here that owners report resisting creasing without setting powder.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a corrector and a concealer?
faqs.a: A corrector uses color theory to neutralize discoloration before coverage. Peach and orange correctors neutralize dark blue circles. Green correctors neutralize red blemishes. You apply corrector first, then concealer on top. The Maybelline Instant Age Rewind combines both in one step with its peach-toned formula.

faqs.q: How do I apply concealer to blemishes without looking cakey?
faqs.a: Use a small flat brush, apply directly to the center of the blemish, and blend outward using light tapping motions rather than wiping. Applying to a dry blemish (no extra oil) helps. Charlotte Tilbury Magic Away covers most blemishes in one application without building up texture.

faqs.q: Can I use concealer without foundation?
faqs.a: Yes. Spot concealing — covering only specific areas — can look more natural than full-face foundation. The Rare Beauty Liquid Touch and NARS Radiant Creamy have natural-skin finishes that blend into bare skin better than full-coverage formulas.

faqs.q: Does setting powder help concealers last longer?
faqs.a: For creasing under the eyes, yes — owners of Shape Tape and Maybelline report that a light dusting of translucent setting powder buys several more hours of crease-free wear. For blemish coverage, setting powder adds transfer resistance. Use a small brush and apply sparingly — over-powdering makes concealer look dry.

faqs.q: How long should I wait after applying eye cream before concealer?
faqs.a: Two to three minutes. Eye cream needs to absorb before you apply product on top — if you skip this step, the concealer slides because the cream underneath hasn't set. This is the most common cause of faster creasing that has nothing to do with the formula itself.
